title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线不是某个新模型，而是 AI 正在把“哪里做事、谁来做事、怎么做生意”一起改写。Aaron Levie 看到 agent 带来的生产力差距还在扩大，Andrej Karpathy 则用 Claude Code 三分钟做出一个 4.7 万条视频的个人项目；另一边，数据中心容量、开放协议和融资话术，提醒我们技术跃迁最终都会落到基础设施和组织选择上。

archive.title: Agent 重写日报
archive.desc: AI agent 正把个人工作流、软件生产力和基础设施版图同时推向新的分水岭。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-11-08 source feeds.

sections.title: The New Builder Workflow / 新的 Builder 工作流
sections.desc: 当 agent 能把想法直接变成可用的产品，个人开发者的瓶颈开始从写代码转向选择问题和组织上下文。

rewrite: Andrej Karpathy turned Tristan's recommended YouTube channels into TristanTube: 47,000 nerdy videos with a TV mode, built in one shot with Claude Code in three minutes. The interesting part is not the toy app; it is the collapsing distance between a personal idea and a working media product. The new advantage is increasingly about knowing what you want to make and supplying the right context, not having a large engineering team.
original:
Earlier this week Tristan published his top YouTube channels:
https://t.co/NZ3UCNo6cT
Which looked excellent so clearly I had to turn it into TristanTube:
https://t.co/l0KyW1WdNH

rewrite: Andrej Karpathy 把 Tristan 推荐的 YouTube 频道做成了 TristanTube：4.7 万条偏 nerdy 的视频，加上适合躺着看的 TV mode，而且是用 Claude Code 三分钟一把梭做出来的。重点不在这个小产品本身，而在于“一个想法到能用的媒体产品”之间的距离正在迅速缩短。新的优势越来越不是拥有大工程团队，而是知道自己想做什么，并能给 agent 足够好的上下文。

rewrite: Builder Zara Zhang pushes back on startup fatalism: an idea's market is not its destiny. With a thousand ways to execute and a hundred different people approaching the same problem, strong execution can create a market that looked nonexistent beforehand. It is a useful reminder for the agent era too: cheaper building increases the value of judgment and iteration, rather than making the original idea irrelevant.
original:
So many people speak of startup as if their fates are predestined: X idea will never work out; the market for Y is too niche...

But startups' fates are MADE, not predetermined. Given one idea, there are 1000 ways to execute it, 100 people will have 100 different approaches. Brilliant people with brilliant execution often create something when there was nothing, or make the impossible seem obvious in hindsight.

rewrite: Builder Zara Zhang 反对一种很常见的创业宿命论：一个想法的市场并不是提前写好的。面对同一个问题，有 1000 种执行方式，也会有 100 个人给出 100 种路径，真正强的执行甚至能凭空做出一个原本不存在的市场。到了 agent 时代，这个判断仍然成立：建造成本下降后，判断力和迭代速度反而更值钱。
original:
很多人谈创业时，好像命运早就注定了：某个想法永远不会成功，某个市场太小……

但创业公司的命运是做出来的，不是预先决定的。同一个想法有 1000 种执行方式，100 个人会有 100 种不同做法。优秀的人加上优秀的执行，常常能从无到有，或者让不可能在事后看起来显而易见。

sections.title: Agent Productivity Has a Location / Agent 生产力的新坐标
sections.desc: 生产力提升不只发生在模型里，也发生在工作流、部署方式和数据中心的地理选择里。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie says coding teams are beginning to see productivity gains one or two orders of magnitude above pre-AI output. The catch is that this requires a real harness, deep domain knowledge, a relatively clean codebase, fluency with multiple agents, and low-friction testing and deployment. The gap is not closing because experienced teams are learning a new operating model while the models themselves take on larger, harder problems.
original:
This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI.

With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding.

What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems.

Right now this is most pronounced in software engineering for the obvious reasons. But there’s no reason we don’t start to see this in a number of other computer-use-sensitive domains like other scientific fields, AEC, finance, cyber, and more. Going to get quite wild.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 说，coding 团队已经开始出现比 AI 之前高一个甚至两个数量级的生产力提升。前提是你得有合适的 harness、深厚的领域理解、相对干净的 codebase、同时驾驭多个 agent 的能力，以及几乎没有摩擦的测试和部署流程。差距没有缩小，是因为有经验的团队在换一套工作操作系统，而模型也在持续接手更大、更难的问题。
original:
这听起来很极端，如果是一年前我也不会相信，但我们开始看到很多例子：生产力比 AI 前高一个甚至两个数量级。

有合适的 harness、对要构建的领域有深入理解、可能还需要一个相对较新的 codebase（当然也有例外）、熟练地同时使用多个 agent，并且测试和部署的摩擦很低，coding 达到这种产出水平是现实的。

疯狂的是，这个差距似乎没有随着时间缩小。你可能以为 AI 会让两条线收敛，但事实是，你过去越有深度，现在越愿意换一种方式，杠杆就越大。随着模型能处理更大、更难的问题，这种优势还会复利。

现在软件工程里最明显，但其他适合电脑操作的领域，比如科学、AEC、金融、网络安全，也没有理由不会出现类似变化。会变得非常疯狂。

rewrite: Levie's infrastructure argument is easy to miss: long-running agents do not need to sit next to the user. Because the work can be encrypted, processed temporarily, and returned as a result, inference can happen in remote 'AI factories' where latency matters less than task value. That widens the map for data-center investment, while countries that refuse to build capacity may simply give up part of the next production layer.
original:
The interesting thing about AI agents is that as a theoretical matter, their inference can kind of run anywhere. AI is one of the few areas of technology that isn’t *as* sensitive to latency back to the user.

Long running agents are now going to be the norm, which means it’s ok to send off work to an AI factory somewhere and that work can essentially be largely done within that remote data center and a final result spit back to the user. The data can pass into these systems in an encrypted manner, be combed through by agents, and then disregarded right after.

And because the economic value of the task is so high relative to the latency sensitivity (eg getting back $500 in value from an automated task, but it takes an extra second to return), you don’t have to have the inference to be particularly close to the user.

Also, because inference is a temporary process with no sensitive data needing to be stored long term where the inference is happening, you can effectively treat AI factories as ephemeral systems, changing some of the data residency dynamics slightly.

Combined, this means you have more flexibility in where you can begin to deploy AI data centers. This is both a huge economic opportunity for the states or countries (or space) that want to take advantage of this fact. And it’s a loss to the states or countries that decide to forgo the opportunity.

rewrite: Levie 的基础设施判断很容易被忽略：长时间运行的 agent 不需要部署在用户身边。只要数据可以加密传入、临时处理、完成后返回结果，inference 就能放在远程的“AI 工厂”里，因为任务价值往往比那一点延迟更重要。这会扩大数据中心投资的地理版图，而选择不建设算力容量的国家，可能等于主动放弃下一层生产力。
original:
有意思的是，从理论上说，AI agent 的 inference 几乎可以在任何地方运行。AI 是少数对返回用户的延迟没那么敏感的技术。

长时间运行的 agent 会成为常态，这意味着可以把工作发到某个地方的 AI 工厂，主要在远程数据中心完成，再把最终结果返回给用户。数据可以加密传入，让 agent 处理完后立即丢弃。

而且任务的经济价值相对延迟敏感度很高，比如一个自动化任务能带来 500 美元价值，但晚一秒返回，所以 inference 不必离用户很近。

因为 inference 是临时过程，处理地点不需要长期保存敏感数据，你可以把 AI 工厂看成短暂存在的系统，这会稍微改变数据驻留的逻辑。

综合来看，部署 AI 数据中心的地点会更灵活。愿意利用这一点的州、国家，甚至太空，都有巨大的经济机会；选择放弃的地方则会损失机会。

sections.title: Capacity, Openness and the Frontier / 容量、开放与前沿
sections.desc: 模型能力的上限，正在同时受到算力供给和开放边界的约束。

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal makes a simple capacity bet: if data-center construction gets harder while demand for compute keeps rising, existing hyperscaler capacity becomes strategically valuable. The likely bottleneck is not appetite for models but the rate at which new training can happen. In his framing, policy may end up pacing the frontier by constraining the physical layer.
original:
If building datacenters becomes harder, it is obvious that you should be super long anyone who has existing capacity (aka hyperscalers).

It's not like the demand for the spice is going way -- it is only continuing to go up.

Thus the spice holders will win big.

What will suffer is the rate of new model training.

I guess we will pace the frontier after all. The body politic speaketh.

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal 押注的是一个很朴素的容量逻辑：如果数据中心越来越难建，而算力需求继续上涨，那么手里已有容量的 hyperscaler 会变得更有战略价值。真正的瓶颈可能不是大家对模型的胃口，而是新一轮训练能以多快的速度发生。换句话说，政策可能会通过物理基础设施来决定前沿推进的速度。
original:
如果建数据中心变得更难，那么显然应该看多那些拥有现有容量的人（也就是 hyperscaler）。

对算力的需求并没有下降，反而还在继续上升。

所以掌握算力的人会大赚。

受影响的会是新模型训练的速度。

看来我们最终还是会由政治来决定前沿的节奏。政治体发言了。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger argues that the Asahi project mattered because it opened something that had been closed and restricted. His objection is to adding new restrictions that make it harder for other projects to build on top of that work. For the builder ecosystem, the point is practical: openness is not only a licensing ideal, but a compounding advantage when many downstream projects need to experiment.
original:
The Asahi project was all about taking something closed and restricted and opening it up.

Adding new restrictions that make it harder for other projects to build on that is not the way. And that AI rejection is just silly. https://t.co/fT4O4wieQm

rewrite: Peter Steinberger 认为，Asahi 项目的价值就在于把一个封闭、受限制的东西打开。他反对的是在此基础上再加新的限制，让其他项目更难继续构建。对 builder 生态来说，这个判断很实际：开放不只是许可证层面的理想，也是一种复利优势，因为越多下游项目能试验，基础层就越容易长出新用法。
original:
Asahi 项目做的就是把一个封闭、受限制的东西打开。

再加上新的限制，让其他项目更难基于它构建，这不是正确的方向。而且那个 AI rejection 简直荒谬。https://t.co/fT4O4wieQm

sections.title: The Startup Theater / 创业融资剧场
sections.desc: 当 AI 让生产和传播都变快，融资叙事也更容易被复制；识别套路，反而成了基本能力。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari's satire on raising a Series A is funny because every step is recognizable: vague revenue charts, launch videos, purchased-looking coverage, fashionable AI phrases, and no deck or data room because the company is supposedly not raising. His parenthetical is the real point: the whole script is satire, but each line is individually true. In a market full of AI theater, the ability to separate signal from performance is part of diligence.
original:
ok here’s how we get investors to fomo our series A and get seven term sheets..

first, we have to vague post revenue. or customers. this is absolutely critical. no y axis, just keep showing numbers and to the right. graphs work and of course get your investors to quote tweet it and take credit. they love doing that anyway. make it vague like “slowly but surely” or “i see an exponential when I see one”

ok, once you do that, you know you can do another launch video for features or even better multiple for features so you get maximum airtime. after that case studies are critical - get a trendsetter company to talk about you or even better have the labs mention you in articles. this will guarantee cold emails to grab coffee from partners.

also you know you can buy “articles” in “premier” publications. you can even run ads against it targeted to just investors too. you’re joking? no dead serious bro.

ok now that you have interest and top of mindshare - the most important thing is to use the magic mantras of “large ambition” and combinations of “long horizon agent swarms abilterared world models physical ai”.

and finally and most importantly you don’t have a deck because of course we’re not raising, we were thinking early next year. and of course we still got pre empted so we don’t have a data room even. you get on or not it’s your call.

and then you use the magic words of optimizing for the best partner but let’s be honest we both know i just want the best valuation.

(again the whole thing is satire, but individually each line is true)

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 调侃 Series A 融资的段子之所以好笑，是因为每一步都似曾相识：模糊的收入曲线、连续的 launch video、看起来像买来的媒体报道、时髦的 AI 关键词，以及“我们没在融资所以没有 deck 和 data room”。他最后的括号才是重点：整套流程是讽刺，但每一句单独看都是真的。在 AI 叙事越来越容易批量生产的市场里，能把信号和表演分开，本身就是尽调能力。
original:
好，现在来说说我们如何让投资人对我们的 Series A FOMO，拿到七份 term sheet……

首先，我们得模糊地发收入，或者客户数。这绝对关键。不放 y 轴，只要数字一直向右走。图表最好用，当然还要让投资人 quote tweet，顺便让他们邀功，他们很喜欢这么做。要写得模糊一点，比如“慢慢但坚定地增长”或“我一看到它就知道是指数增长”。

然后你可以再拍一个 feature launch video，最好多个，这样能获得最大曝光。接着 case study 很关键，让一家趋势公司出来谈你，最好让那些 labs 在文章里提到你。这样 partner 就会发冷邮件约咖啡。

还有，你知道你可以买“顶级”媒体的“文章”，甚至可以只针对投资人投广告。你以为我在开玩笑？不，哥们，认真的。

一旦有了关注度，最重要的就是使用“宏大愿景”，以及“长周期 agent swarm、颠覆世界模型、physical AI”之类的组合。

最后最重要的是，你当然没有 deck，因为我们根本没在融资，只是明年年初可能会考虑。然后我们还被提前投资了，所以也没有 data room。上不上车随你。

然后你再说，我们在为最好的合作伙伴优化，但说实话，我们都知道我只是想要最高估值。

（再说一次，整件事是讽刺，但每一行单独看都是真的）
